title: AI R&D-relevant model capabilities are improving rapidly and are getting harder to measure
summary: Contents Overview 1 Background 2 Methodology 3 Results 4 Robustness Checks 5 Discussion 6 Acknowledgments Appendices A Difficulty Estimation and Baselining B Time Horizon Diagnostics C MCI Modelling Methodology D Limitations of IRT E MCI Robustness Checks F Estimating Lifecycle Cost for Tasks G Data Integrity and Reward Hacking H Changes in Capability Growth Rates I Inference Scaling J Swarm Experiments K Al Zimmermann's Programming Contests L Budget NanoGPT M Making METR tasks N Earthborne Rangers and Continual Learning O Qualitative and External Evidence on Models’ Strengths and Limitations Overview This post presents evidence from our capability evaluations of public models relevant to AI R&D acceleration, up to Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra. We remain significantly uncertain about central questions, including (1) what capabilities are in practice necessary for drastic acceleration, and (2) how quickly relevant model capabilities are improving. We think that current public evidence is insufficient to rule out drastic AI R&D acceleration in the next couple of years. By drastic AI R&D acceleration we mean a situation where capabilities improve so quickly that humans are no longer able to meaningfully understand, assess, and react to catastrophic risks posed by new AI systems. title: Depth Pro 2: Sharp and Temporally Consistent Metric Monocular Depth
summary: We present Depth Pro 2, an approach to estimating dense metric depth for images and video at full resolution. By analyzing prior methods for monocular depth estimation, we find that they commonly trade off temporal consistency and boundary sharpness: multi-frame methods favor consistency, single-frame methods favor sharpness. To overcome this trade-off, we train a single, scalable network that processes both images and video and predicts depth maps at native resolution.
